lead.tldr: Fed Chair Warsh confirmed, likely dovish stance could lower rates, supporting crypto risk assets • Schwab launches spot BTC and ETH for 35 million clients, expanding retail exposure and potential inflows • KDDI buys 14.9% of Coincheck for $65 million, linking telecom distribution channels to crypto trading • NUVA marketplace brings $19 billion of tokenized real‑world assets to Ethereum, widening DeFi collateral base • Long‑term holders now control nearly 4 million BTC, tightening liquid supply and creating upside pressure • Tokenized US Treasury TVL exceeds $15 billion, indicating institutional confidence in on‑chain fixed‑income products

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The Senate’s confirmation of a new Fed chair hints at a dovish monetary stance. Meanwhile, record long‑term Bitcoin holdings tighten supply, tokenized assets top $15 billion and Schwab launches spot crypto trading for retail.

top_signals.title: Senate Confirms Kevin Warsh as Next Federal Reserve Chair on Bankless
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as the 17th Chair of the Federal Reserve in a 54-45 partisan vote. The vote was the most contentious Fed chair confirmation in history. Despite Warsh’s prior hawkish reputation, analysts now expect a more dovish monetary policy stance under his leadership. The shift comes as inflation pressures remain high, making the Fed’s policy direction critical for institutional investors.

top_signals.title: Charles Schwab begins rollout of spot BTC, ETH trading for U.S. retail customers
top_signals.summary: Charles Schwab has started rolling out its Schwab Crypto platform that enables U.S. retail customers to trade spot Bitcoin and Ether directly. The service gives Schwab’s roughly 35 million clients direct access to the two largest crypto assets without the need for a separate exchange. This rollout could increase retail participation in crypto markets and support broader mainstream adoption, which may be relevant for institutional investors monitoring demand and liquidity trends.

top_signals.title: Telecom giant KDDI to acquire 14.9% stake in Coincheck Group in $65 million deal
top_signals.summary: Japanese telecom giant KDDI is buying a 14.9% equity stake in crypto exchange operator Coincheck Group for $65 million, acquiring 28.5 million newly issued shares. The transaction includes a business alliance that will allow revenue sharing and customer referrals, enabling KDDI to expand crypto access through its consumer channels. In addition, KDDI will receive the right to nominate a member to Coincheck’s board, giving it influence over the exchange’s strategic direction.

top_signals.title: RWA news: Animoca-backed NUVA brings Figure's $19 billion of tokenized assets to Ethereum
top_signals.summary: Animoca Brands and Nuva Labs have launched NUVA, an Ethereum‑based marketplace for tokenized real‑world assets. The platform will bring roughly $19 billion of assets from Figure Technologies onto decentralized finance. It debuts with a Treasury‑linked yield vault and a token backed by an $18.4 billion home‑equity loan portfolio. The offering expands collateral and investment options for retail participants and signals growing institutional interest in real‑world asset tokenization.

top_signals.title: Tokenized assets reach $15B valuation, Schwab rolls out crypto trading for US customers, KRWQ expands to Solana
top_signals.summary: Tokenized U.S. Treasury assets have now exceeded $15 billion in total value locked, highlighting growing institutional appetite for blockchain‑based fixed‑income exposure. Charles Schwab is beginning to offer spot cryptocurrency trading to its U.S. retail client base, signaling broader acceptance of digital assets by a major brokerage. The KRWQ stablecoin has been deployed on the Solana network to boost on‑chain liquidity for the Korean won, expanding the range of fiat‑backed tokens available to traders. The report also notes a series of recent venture capital rounds in the crypto sector, underscoring continued funding momentum for infrastructure and asset‑tokenization projects.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin's available supply is shrinking as long-term holding hits record 4 million BTC
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin's available supply is decreasing as long‑term holders now control nearly 4 million BTC. This represents a 300 % increase in conviction‑buyer balances since late 2025. The concentration of coins off‑exchange is tightening liquid supply on major trading venues. Analysts note that the resulting supply shock, valued at more than $320 billion, could create significant upside potential for price if demand resurges.

top_signals.title: UK parliament to probe Nigel Farage’s $6.8 million donation from crypto billionaire
top_signals.summary: The UK parliamentary standards watchdog has launched a formal investigation into Reform UK leader Nigel Farage for failing to declare a donation of £5 million (approximately $6.8 million) from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne. Harborne is known for his stake in the stablecoin issuer Tether, linking the case to broader scrutiny of crypto‑related political financing. A finding of a breach of the parliamentary code of conduct could result in Farage’s suspension from the House of Commons, underscoring regulatory risk for political actors receiving crypto‑industry funds.

top_signals.title: The Protocol: Solana’s ‘Alpenglow’ upgrade is live for testing
top_signals.summary: Solana has deployed its Alpenglow consensus upgrade on a community test cluster, representing the largest protocol change in the network’s history. The upgrade is intended to improve scalability and security as the platform prepares for broader adoption. In related ecosystem news LayerZero apologized for its involvement in the $292 million Kelp DAO exploit while Ronin disclosed a migration to an Ethereum layer‑2 solution. The Ethereum Foundation also announced a new Clear Signing standard aimed at preventing malicious transaction approvals.

top_signals.title: Joe Lubin's Consensys has delayed its potential IPO until fall
top_signals.summary: Consensys, the Ethereum infrastructure firm founded by Joe Lubin, has postponed its planned U.S. initial public offering until the fall, citing weak market conditions. The company had been targeting a draft S‑1 filing with the SEC by the end of February 2026. Consensys previously raised $450 million in a 2022 Series D financing round. The delay aligns with recent postponements by other crypto companies such as Kraken and Ledger, underscoring the sector’s sensitivity to market volatility.

top_signals.title: Coinbase (COIN) backs Hyperliquid (HYPE) stablecoin push as DeFi trading volumes climb
top_signals.summary: Coinbase will serve as the official treasury deployer of USDC on Hyperliquid’s DeFi trading platform, giving it the right to acquire assets tied to Hyperliquid’s native stablecoin USDH. The agreement also includes Circle expanding USDC usage on Hyperliquid and committing to stake 500,000 HYPE tokens. By linking a major custodial exchange’s treasury to a decentralized stablecoin, the partnership signals increased institutional confidence in on‑chain liquidity provision. The move comes as DeFi trading volumes are climbing, highlighting the strategic importance of stablecoin integration for large‑scale investors.

top_signals.title: Unpacking Aave: Quantifying the Leverage in DeFi
top_signals.summary: Galaxy Research has examined Aave’s loan book following the recent $290 million KelpDAO exploit. The exploit created $123 million of bad debt on Aave and drove utilization on its core lending pools close to 100 percent. The analysis underscores a systemic leverage risk that could affect broader DeFi lending stability. It also references the DeFi United initiative’s intention to raise more than $300 million to address the shortfall.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The past week reminded us how quickly the crypto ecosystem can shift under the influence of both policy and mainstream finance. In Washington, the Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as the 17th Chair of the Federal Reserve. While his reputation was once seen as hawkish, market analysts now anticipate a softer monetary stance. For institutional investors, that potential pivot could reshape risk appetite and capital allocation across digital assets. Across the Atlantic, Charles Schwab launched its Schwab Crypto platform, giving roughly 35 million retail clients direct access to spot Bitcoin and Ether. No separate exchange is required, and the move signals a growing confidence among traditional brokers to bring crypto into everyday portfolios. We at Blockwall see this as a clear sign that retail demand will continue to rise, feeding liquidity that benefits both early‑stage projects and larger ecosystem players. In Asia, telecom giant KDDI announced a $65 million investment for a 14.9 percent stake in Coincheck Group. The partnership includes revenue sharing and customer referrals, allowing KDDI to embed crypto services into its consumer channels. A board seat also gives KDDI a voice in the exchange’s strategic direction, highlighting how non‑financial firms are becoming key stakeholders in the crypto space. These developments raise a crucial question for founders building the next wave of Web3 infrastructure: how will you position your business to capture the opportunities created by shifting monetary policy, expanding retail access, and strategic corporate alliances? #Web3 #Crypto #Blockchain #CryptoVC
